comparisons.peer_topic: Data center and cloud computing solutions
comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers a deep portfolio of data center solutions including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, SmartNICs, and FPGAs to meet performance requirements for data centers, supercomputers, and cloud environments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD describe core offerings to modernize and manage enterprise IT infrastructure, but they focus on different layers of the stack. AVGO focuses on the software and networking fabric layer, stating its software 'help enterprises simplify their information technology ("IT") environments' and 'manage... hybrid cloud environments,' while also offering 'fibre channel storage area networking ("FC SAN") products.' In contrast, AMD focuses on the underlying silicon compute layer, offering 'data center computing solutions including AI accelerators, microprocessors (CPUs), graphic processing units (GPUs)... to meet the vast computing performance requirements of today's data centers... and cloud environments.' AVGO provides the integration and management layer for the environment, whereas AMD provides the high-performance processing engines within that environment.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions help enterprises simplify their information technology ("IT") environments so they can increase business velocity and flexibility, and enable customers to plan, develop, deliver, automate, manage, and secure applications across mainframe, distributed, edge, mobile, and private and hybrid cloud platforms.

Many of the largest companies in the world, including most of the Fortune 500, and many government agencies rely on our software solutions to help manage and secure their on-premises and hybrid cloud environments, private cloud infrastructure and AI data centers.

We also offer mission-critical fibre channel storage area networking ("FC SAN") products and related software in the form of modules, switches and subsystems incorporating multiple semiconductor products.

We offer a deep portfolio of data center computing solutions including AI accelerators, microprocessors (CPUs), graphic processing units (GPUs), data processing units (DPUs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs), and field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), to meet the vast computing performance requirements of today's data centers, supercomputers, AI and Machine Learning (ML) data center environments and cloud environments.

comparisons.peer_summary: Beyond CPUs, Intel delivers xPU products including GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and accelerators to address diverse workloads and computing needs. The company aims to offer leading products across these different architectural categories.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address diverse computing needs in data centers through broad portfolios, but Intel emphasizes a multi-architecture 'xPU' strategy beyond traditional CPUs, while AVGO emphasizes software-defined infrastructure and security. Intel states it delivers 'a family of xPU products encompassing client and data center GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and other accelerators' to meet 'diverse computing needs.' AVGO, conversely, highlights its 'infrastructure and security software' designed to 'modernize, optimize, and secure the most complex private and hybrid cloud environments,' alongside 'FC SAN' hardware. The similarity lies in serving the data center market with specialized hardware/software solutions; the difference is Intel's focus on silicon diversity (xPU) versus AVGO's focus on connectivity, storage, and security orchestration software.

sentences.text: Our portfolio of industry-leading infrastructure and security software is designed to modernize, optimize, and secure the most complex private and hybrid cloud environments, enabling scalability, agility, automation, insights, resiliency and security, making it easy for customers to run their mission-critical workloads.

We also offer mission-critical fibre channel storage area networking ("FC SAN") products and related software in the form of modules, switches and subsystems incorporating multiple semiconductor products.
Beyond the CPU, we deliver a family of xPU products encompassing client and data center GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and other accelerators.
The xPU approach recognizes that different workloads benefit from different computing architectures, and our broad portfolio helps meet our customers' increasingly diverse computing needs.

comparisons.peer_summary: Micron is an industry leader in innovative memory and storage solutions, delivering high-performance DRAM, NAND, and NOR products through Micron® and Crucial® brands to enable advances in AI and compute-intensive applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and Micron identify AI and data-intensive applications as key drivers for their products, but they occupy different positions in the supply chain. Micron is a leader in 'memory and storage solutions... to enable advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and compute-intensive applications,' providing the raw memory (DRAM/NAND) substrate. AVGO provides the infrastructure software and 'FC SAN' products that 'help enterprises simplify their IT environments' to 'manage... AI data centers.' While Micron supplies the storage media, AVGO supplies the networking and management software to organize and secure those workloads in hybrid cloud and data center environments.

Every day, the innovations that our people create fuel the data economy, enabling advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and compute-intensive applications that unleash opportunities - from the data center to the intelligent edge and across the client and mobile user experience.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA offers Omniverse as a development platform for virtual world simulations, with industrial enterprises adopting its 3D and simulation technologies to digitalize assets and build digital twins of physical environments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVIDIA describe platforms that help enterprises manage and simulate complex physical or digital environments, though their core technologies differ. NVIDIA offers 'Omniverse... for building virtual world simulation applications' to help enterprises 'build digital twins of factories.' AVGO offers 'infrastructure software solutions' that 'help enterprises simplify their information technology ("IT") environments' and 'manage... on-premises and hybrid cloud environments.' Both provide enterprise-grade tools to bring order and simulation capabilities to complex IT/physical infrastructures, with NVDA focusing on 3D simulation/digital twins and AVGO focusing on IT workload management and storage networking.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions help enterprises simplify their information technology ("IT") environments so they can increase business velocity and flexibility, and enable customers to plan, develop, deliver, automate, manage, and secure applications across mainframe, distributed, edge, mobile, and private and hybrid cloud platforms.

Many of the largest companies in the world, including most of the Fortune 500, and many government agencies rely on our software solutions to help manage and secure their on-premises and hybrid cloud environments, private cloud infrastructure and AI data centers.

We offer NVIDIA Omniverse as a development platform and operating system for building virtual world simulation applications, available as a software subscription for enterprise use and free for individual use.

Industrial enterprises are adopting Omniverse's 3D and simulation technologies to digitalize their complex physical assets, processes, and environments - building digital twins of factories, real time 3D product configurators, testing and validating autonomous robots and vehicles, powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure on-premises and in the cloud.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies emphasize the integration of AI into their core platforms, but at different scopes: AVGO integrates AI capabilities into enterprise software for managing cloud environments, while QCOM integrates AI into mobile/edge hardware processors. QCOM's 'Qualcomm AI Engine... includes dedicated hardware capable of running complex AI use cases... on device,' leveraging 'Oryon and Kryo CPU processors.' AVGO's infrastructure software 'help enterprises... automate, manage, and secure applications across... private and hybrid cloud platforms' and 'enable customers to... manage... AI data centers.' Both leverage AI to enhance performance and automation, but QCOM focuses on on-device/edge AI inference via SoCs, whereas AVGO focuses on centralized data center IT management and security.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions help enterprises simplify their information technology ("IT") environments so they can increase business velocity and flexibility, and enable customers to plan, develop, deliver, automate, manage, and secure applications across mainframe, distributed, edge, mobile, and private and hybrid cloud platforms.

Our portfolio of industry-leading infrastructure and security software is designed to modernize, optimize, and secure the most complex private and hybrid cloud environments, enabling scalability, agility, automation, insights, resiliency and security, making it easy for customers to run their mission-critical workloads.

The Qualcomm® AI Engine, featured in our Snapdragon platforms and many of our other products, includes dedicated hardware capable of running complex AI use cases at high-performance and low-power on device, while also enhancing privacy and security.
In addition to our leading AI technology, we are simplifying the process for developers to build applications with AI features to work on our Snapdragon platforms.
